The goal of these materials is to make statistics useful and understandable through real questions, careful interpretation, and opportunities to explore ideas. The first learning collection centers on Elementary Statistics, with examples drawn from psychology, behavioral health, and everyday research.

### Understanding data and uncertainty

Explore a proposed 18-week sequence from describing distributions and sampling to confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, group comparisons, correlation, and regression.

The hub organizes learning objectives, laboratory and project work, and planned interactive demonstrations. **The course design is a sample; no completed interactive lessons are published yet.**

## Learning resources in development

The resources below follow the proposed syllabus. Each future lesson will connect a short explanation to a prediction, a worked example or demonstration, and an interpretation question.

| Topic | Proposed week(s) | Planned activity |
|---|---|---|
| Understanding distributions | 3–4 | Explore how outliers and distribution shape affect numerical summaries |
| Sampling distributions | 6 | Compare the distribution of sample means at different sample sizes |
| Confidence intervals | 7 | Investigate the long-run coverage of repeated-sample intervals |
| Hypothesis tests and power | 8 | Explore effects of sample size, variability, and effect size |
| Correlation and regression | 14–15 | Examine association, prediction, outliers, and causal limitations |

These activities will be developed as browser-based learning resources with keyboard-accessible controls, readable explanations, and appropriate nonvisual alternatives. Grades and student submissions will remain in institutional course systems.

## Teaching approach

I approach teaching as an opportunity to develop reasoning, not only technical proficiency.

- **Begin with questions.** Use meaningful examples to connect statistical ideas to real research and decisions.
- **Build understanding step by step.** Combine clear explanations, worked examples, guided practice, and timely feedback.
- **Interpret findings responsibly.** Examine study design, measurement, assumptions, uncertainty, bias, generalizability, and practical importance.
- **Design for access.** Provide multiple ways to engage with concepts and avoid assuming prior experience with statistical software or programming.

## Instruction and mentorship

Since 2016, I have contributed instruction in research methods and program evaluation to the doctoral psychology internship training program at Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services.

In partnership with the training team, I guide approximately four doctoral interns each year through a yearlong applied research or evaluation project. Instruction and ongoing feedback cover literature review, study design, measurement, statistical analysis, interpretation, scholarly writing, and formal presentations. The goal is to build independence while connecting methodological rigor with practical organizational questions.

This experience is **distinct from a formal college teaching appointment**.

## Sample course design and related scholarship

The proposed learning collection is based on an **Elementary Statistics (PSYC 210) sample syllabus for Cerritos College**, created as an instructional design example rather than an active or officially adopted section. Course requirements would be finalized with the approved Course Outline of Record and the department.

My [research publications](research.qmd) and [conference presentations](presentations.qmd) also provide examples of data interpretation, applied evaluation, and communicating evidence.
